A chambers meeting in the case of Sirhan Bishara Sirhan was recorded on May 16, 1969. Sirhan stood convicted of assassinating Senator Robert F. Kennedy. The meeting was held before Assistant Presiding Judge Charles A. Loring, in the Superior Court of California for Los Angeles County. Judge Herbert V. Walker, who had presided at the trial, was present. So were Los Angeles Police Deputy Chief Robert Houghton and Deputy District Attorney David Fitts.

Chambers meetings settle what the jury never hears: procedure, security, and the handling of a famous defendant. A transcript of one, kept in full, shows judges and prosecutors managing the case's machinery after the verdict. The names and offices are all on the record. It is a primary scrap of court administration from the Sirhan case.
